result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Answer A says plainly that the form is already sound and names the specific things that work. It keeps the markup almost unchanged and ties each small edit to the person filling in the form: 16px text stops iPhones zooming in, and the 44px button is easy to tap. Answer B is careful and keeps the backend contract intact, but it never says the original form was good, it rewrites the styling heavily, and it adds decoration such as a card, a shadow and transitions. B's accessibility points (focus rings, :user-invalid) are useful, but most of its changes are visual polish rather than fixes for users. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): B says plainly that the form is already sound and names what works: visible labels, correct input types and autocomplete, the optional field marked in words, and a specific button label. Its few edits each have a clear user-facing reason: 16px text so iPhones don't zoom in, a 44px button that's easy to tap, and box-sizing so fields fit the width. A restyles the whole form with a card, shadow, wrapper divs and a brand-colored button without saying what already worked. It keeps the labels and the optional marking intact, and some changes (focus rings, :user-invalid) do help users, but much of the rest is decoration answering 'more professional'.
